strengths: Well-motivated training-free approach that addresses a real trade-off between computational cost and reasoning coverage, with compelling motivation for soft geometry over hard constraints

Strong and consistent empirical results: up to 13-point AUC improvements across 7 benchmarks (math and code) on Qwen3-8B with only 1.1-1.3× overhead, outperforming both training-free sampling and RL-tuned baselines

Comprehensive experimental analysis including component ablations (Table 3), training stage effects (Figure 5), mode collapse visualization (Figure 4), and cost-robustness frontier analysis (Figure 3)

Sound technical design: tangent-space sampling correctly preserves manifold structure, chunk-wise KV cache resets elegantly maintain linear memory, and fixed random projections keep the method training-free
Clear algorithmic presentation (Algorithm 1) and generally well-written paper with effective visualizations of key concepts
weaknesses: Incomplete paper with critical implementation details missing: multiple unresolved appendix references ('Appendix ??', 'Table ??', 'Figure ??'), projection matrices W, Aℓ, Bℓ not fully specified, and key hyperparameter justifications deferred to unavailable sections, severely impacting reproducibility

Limited technical novelty: latent anchors resemble Delethink, soft regularization is standard, and chunk-based generation is not new; the contribution amounts to an empirical combination of three regularizers lacking principled justification

No theoretical grounding for design choices: why this specific combination of foresight + bumpiness + uniformity? Why is single-sample rollout sufficient for ranking? Bumpiness penalty (Eq. 5) measures within-rollout smoothness, not cross-chunk coherence after KV cache resets. Hyperparameter choices (λb, λu, δ=0.2, r=8) appear ad-hoc

Narrow evaluation scope: primarily Qwen3-8B only, limited to two model families (Qwen3, Phi-4), no evaluation on other major models (Claude, Llama, Gemini), restricted to math/code domains, and no validation on truly long-context benchmarks despite claims about long-context reasoning

Questionable comparison fairness: 'Avg. Tokens' metric conflates generation and rollout tokens across methods, K=8 candidate rollouts per boundary is substantial compute yet unclear if baselines receive matched budgets, RL training costs not directly compared, and no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Technical concerns: state extraction using only <EOC> hidden state (Eq. 1) may lose chunk-level information without justification; latency overhead acknowledged but dismissed despite being significant for practical deployment; 'linear memory' claim (Section 3.1) doesn't fully account for context window S=512; hard geometry analysis doesn't rigorously explain why soft penalties specifically help

Limited analysis and missing evidence: Figure 4 (left) uses PCA for visualization without validating it captures semantic diversity; missing Table ?? on latent statistics (Neff); no failure case analysis; interesting observation about smaller gains on RL-optimized models (Figure 5) deserves deeper investigation but receives only passing mention

No code release mentioned and insufficient detail for reproduction: hyperparameter sensitivity only analyzed for K and s (Figure 4 right), initialization of random matrices unspecified, exact sampling configuration unclear despite temperature=0.6 mention, key design choices not ablated

strengths: Training-free inference-time search avoids expensive RL training while achieving competitive empirical results across multiple benchmarks (MATH500, AIME25, OlympiadBench, OmniMath, HumanEval, BigCodeBench, LiveCodeBench)
Comprehensive evaluation across model scales (1.7B-14B) and systematic ablations (Table 3) demonstrate each component contributes to performance
Valid technical insight (Section 3.5) that hard geometric constraints suffer exponential acceptance decay in high dimensions, motivating soft regularization approach
Well-structured pipeline with clear motivation for chunk-based search with KV cache resets to maintain linear memory complexity
Insightful analysis of mode diversity (Figure 4 left) showing RL baselines collapse into narrow latent regions while TGR maintains dispersed distributions
weaknesses: Severe presentation failures with broken references throughout ('Appendix ??' appears 8+ times), missing critical implementation details (W initialization, A_ℓ/B_ℓ sampling distribution, token counting methodology), and inaccessible appendices, making reproduction impossible and suggesting incomplete submission

Contradictory 'matched budget' claims: stated as 'negligible' 1.1-1.3× overhead yet data shows TGR uses 16.7% more tokens than PSampling on AIME25 (7.0k vs 6.0k) with variable token costs across methods, undermining central efficiency claims
No statistical significance testing, error bars, or confidence intervals reported; single runs on small benchmarks (AIME25 has only 24 problems) where differences could be within noise

Unjustified design choices: unit-norm anchors assumed without establishing manifold hypothesis, bumpiness penalty (Eq. 5) formulation ad-hoc, uniformity penalty (Eq. 6) threshold δ=0.2 not principled, single Monte Carlo sample for expectations coarse

Limited novelty: straightforward combination of existing techniques (latent search, KV caching, soft regularization) with no novel components; each element is standard, and overall contribution is incremental

Weak experimental analysis: Figure 4 left uses only 2D PCA visualization to claim mode collapse (lossy dimensionality reduction, no quantitative metrics); supporting Table ?? is missing; TGR-Token underperforms Dele-Token by 1.6 AUC points without explanation of fairness

Reduced applicability shown in Figure 5: method provides substantial gains on SFT models but narrow improvements on RL-tuned models, suggesting limited utility for state-of-the-art reasoning models; analysis lacks depth

Critical missing details prevent reproducibility: projection matrix W initialization unspecified, residual injection matrices A_ℓ/B_ℓ distribution and rank r=8 choice unexplained, hyperparameter tuning procedure and validation set construction unclear, no code availability mentioned

Strong and comprehensive empirical results across 7 benchmarks with AUC improvements up to 13 points and competitive token efficiency
Principled theoretical motivation for soft geometric regularization over hard constraints via concentration of measure analysis (Section 3.5)
Thorough experimental analysis including ablations (Table 3), mode collapse visualization (Figure 4), and training stage dependencies (Figure 5)
Practical chunk-wise KV cache reset design maintaining linear memory complexity without architectural modifications
Consistent improvements across both math (MATH500, AIME, OlympiadBench, OmniMath) and code (HumanEval, BigCodeBench, LiveCodeBench) benchmarks
Clear presentation with effective visual explanations and well-structured methodology description
weaknesses: Manuscript incompleteness: multiple critical references to missing Appendices and Figures (???) severely impairs reproducibility and evaluation

Excellent reproducibility: complete hyperparameters, implementation details in appendices, multiple seeds, and end-to-end token accounting
Insightful analyses of mode collapse (Table 13), training-stage effects on inference-time controllability (Figure 5), and efficiency frontier dominance (Figure 3)
Well-designed technical framework with principled scoring function combining look-ahead utility, trajectory smoothness, and diversity
Comprehensive supplementary material covering theory, failure taxonomy, qualitative cases, and sensitivity analyses
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: combines existing techniques (chunk-based generation, soft regularization, KV resets) rather than introducing fundamental innovations
Oversold 'manifold-informed' framing: soft regularizers don't directly model manifold geometry; connection to differential geometry is loose and largely heuristic

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 7 benchmarks, 4 model scales (1.7B-14B), with consistent improvements in AUC (up to 13 points on Qwen3-8B)
Practical training-free design with modest 1.1-1.3× overhead; clear engineering contributions including O(S) KV memory bound via chunk-wise resets
Thorough analysis and honest discussion of limitations, including failure modes (delayed utility), training-stage dependency, and latent-space geometry diagnostics
Strong presentation with detailed ablations (Table 3), sensitivity analyses (Tables 4, 8), geometric characterization (Table 13, Figures 6, 13), and implementation details
Extends across both math and code domains with consistent patterns; scaling analysis shows benefits hold from 1.7B to 14B parameters
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: combines straightforward techniques (chunking, latent extraction, look-ahead, soft regularization) without principled justification. The 'manifold-informed' framing is oversold—soft penalties are generic regularizers applicable to any continuous space

Weak theoretical motivation: no justification for why normalized EOC hidden states represent reasoning state; unit-sphere projection's information loss unclaimed; transition from hard to soft geometry (§3.5) appears pragmatic rather than principled. Fixed random projection W suboptimal vs learned alternatives

Critical training-stage dependency: Method shows large gains on SFT models but degrades significantly (or fails) on RL-tuned models (Figure 5: Phi-4-reasoning-plus MATH500 shows -0.3 AUC). This severely limits applicability in modern deployments where models are RL-optimized

Shallow rollout horizon and unresolved delayed utility: Rollouts cover only ~6-12% of chunk length (s=32-64 vs S=512). Case 3 identifies failure mode where decisive signals lie beyond horizon. Proposed mitigation ('selective deepening') unimplemented and unquantified

Questionable comparison fairness: (1) TGR spends inference tokens while RL baselines amortized training cost—comparing on matched tokens conflates different resource types; (2) Hyperparameter tuning of TGR defaults (λb=λu=0.5, K=8) on evaluation sets unchecked; (3) AUC metric on log scale may systematically favor diversity-focused methods

Limited single-sample performance improvements: Pass@1 gains are modest (Table 1: +9.1 AIME25 @1 vs +10.8 AUC), suggesting improvements are primarily in coverage/diversity rather than solution quality. For single-answer applications, benefits are limited

Context truncation concerns: O(S) memory bound requires aggressive KV reset, discarding history. Impact on performance when reasoning depends on information outside bounded context unclaimed. Ironically may limit long-context reasoning

Unclear design choices: Why is normalized EOC hidden state the right state representation? Why fixed random low-rank injection matrices (r=8) vs learned alternatives? Why these specific soft penalties vs other geometric regularizations? Why fixed-length chunks vs adaptive boundaries? Few alternatives explored

Statistical rigor: Only 3 random seeds reported; no confidence intervals or significance tests despite some modest improvements (e.g., Table 2: HumanEval 56.1→57.1). Unclear which improvements are statistically significant

Limited generalization: Pilot open-ended evaluations (Table 12) weaker than math/code. Method appears optimized for tasks with verifiable correctness; applicability to open-ended generation unclear. Failure taxonomy (Appendix H) mostly symptom descriptions without concrete diagnostics

strengths: Training-free inference-time method enabling broad applicability without weight updates or retraining
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 7 benchmarks, 4 model scales (1.7B-14B), proper baselines with ablations isolating each component's contribution
Insightful analysis of why hard geometric constraints fail in high dimensions (Table 6, exponential decay in feasibility rates), motivating soft regularization approach
Well-engineered design: chunk-wise KV reset achieves O(S) memory bound; tangent-space perturbations preserve manifold structure; overhead of only 1.11-1.13× for significant AUC gains

Excellent latent geometry diagnostics showing TGR maintains 6.5/8 effective candidate diversity vs. 1.2/8 collapse in RL baselines (Table 13); Figure 4 visualization effectively demonstrates mode-collapse problem
Honest limitation discussion with concrete failure case analysis (delayed utility beyond rollout horizon) and systematic failure taxonomy (Appendix H)
Reproducibility and transparency: extensive implementation details, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, full algorithm specification, multiple independent runs
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual components (look-ahead, smoothness, diversity penalties) are standard; contribution is primarily in their combination for latent search, incremental relative to existing test-time scaling methods

Fundamental limitation of shallow rollouts (s=32/64) not adequately addressed: failure Case 3 shows discriminative signals beyond rollout horizon cause incorrect choices; no systematic analysis of failure rates or guidance for when deeper rollouts needed; proposed mitigations (selective deepening) mentioned but not implemented

Narrow applicability: Figure 5 shows gains diminish significantly on RL-optimized models, suggesting method exploits 'residual flexibility' that decreases with training; pilot open-ended evaluations (Table 12) lack rigor; unclear generalization beyond math/code with clear verification signals

KV cache reset trade-offs underexplored: bounded explicit context (length S) risks losing distant information; single continuous anchor per boundary severely compresses multi-chunk state; failure mode acknowledged but not systematically studied

Design choices lack principled justification: why these specific components over alternatives? bumpiness penalty uses discrete second-order differences without principled justification; uniformity threshold δ=0.2 appears arbitrary; single-sample rollout (N_MC=1) creates noise for similar candidates; hinge loss form unexplored
Fixed random matrices seem inelegant: framing as 'training-free' conflates frozen weights with no learning; no analysis of whether learned matrices (with frozen backbone) would improve results
Non-standard overhead accounting: 'forward-token units' may obscure actual wall-clock latency implications critical for deployment; end-to-end latency measurements missing

Limited comparison with structured search methods: ToT/GoT comparisons relegated to appendix with minimal discussion; RL baselines trained on specific benchmarks may not be optimal; broader test-time scaling baseline coverage needed
